scenes.text: The four shapes on a PlayStation controller aren't random. Each one means something. The triangle is a point of view. The square is a sheet of paper, which is why it opens menus. But the circle and the X are the surprise. They're yes and no. In Japan, a circle means correct and an X means wrong, so games there used circle to confirm. Then the console came west, and it flipped. Here, you press X to say yes. A player in Japan would read that as pressing no. Got something you own that you've always wondered about? Comment it below, and it might be my next episode.
